open_questions.q: How does the 2016 reassignment of Propionibacterium acnes, P. avidum, and P. granulosum into the new genus Cutibacterium affect the paper's 'genus-wide' pan-genome and metabolic-diversity claims when the 6-strain panel is re-analyzed under modern taxonomy?
open_questions.basis: The paper works under the 2015-era genus Propionibacterium and treats P. acnes / P. avidum together with P. freudenreichii / P. acidipropionici / P. propionicum as a single genus for pan-genome comparison. Scholz & Kilian (2016, IJSEM) reassigned the cutaneous cluster (acnes, avidum, granulosum) to Cutibacterium. Under modern taxonomy the paper's 'genus-wide' pan-genome is actually a two-genus mixed pan-genome, which is expected to inflate the pan-genome and depress the core.
next_steps: Re-partition the 6 (or expanded 16) strains into Propionibacterium sensu stricto vs. Cutibacterium and re-run the blastp+MCL@1.5 pipeline separately per genus.
Compare within-genus core/pan curves to the mixed-genus curves in the paper to quantify how much of the reported 'open pan-genome' is genus-boundary artifact.
Rerun the M1-M6 pathway audit within each genus; test whether methylmalonyl-CoA mutase remains core to Propionibacterium sensu stricto specifically.

open_questions.q: How does gene-content divergence partition across skin, dairy, and oral niches once the panel is expanded beyond 6 inter-species representatives to the full BV-BRC / RefSeq Propionibacterium + Cutibacterium set?
open_questions.basis: The paper uses 6 inter-species reps for the primary pan-genome comparison and 16 closed genomes for the 65% strain-specific figure. Modern databases (BV-BRC, RefSeq) now hold hundreds of Cutibacterium acnes skin isolates, dozens of P. freudenreichii dairy strains, and increasing P. propionicum oral / P. avidum opportunistic isolates. This raises the empirical question of whether niche is a stronger predictor of accessory-gene content than phylogenetic species assignment.
next_steps: Pull the current BV-BRC Propionibacterium + Cutibacterium closed/complete set stratified by isolation source (skin, dairy, oral, wound/opportunistic).
Compute pan-genome per niche and cross-niche accessory-gene sharing (Jaccard on cluster occupancy).
Fit a mixed-effects model with species and niche as predictors of accessory-gene presence to quantify niche-effect vs. species-effect.

open_questions.q: Does the Wood-Werkman propionate-fermentation pathway show cryptic strain-level variation (e.g. methylmalonyl-CoA mutase paralogs, transcarboxylase subunit composition, PFOR / nifJ isozyme choice) that would explain the observed 4.36 - 9.93 mmol propionate flux spread across the six GEMs?
open_questions.basis: The FBA layer reproduces a nearly 2.3-fold spread in propionate secretion across the six GEMs (PPRO 4.36 vs PACN 9.93 mmol gDW^-1 h^-1). The pathway audit confirms methylmalonyl-CoA mutase is present in all 6 strains at hit-count 2 each, but does not resolve isozyme identity, transcarboxylase subunit stoichiometry, or ferredoxin partner choice - all of which are known regulators of Wood-Werkman flux. The paper does not decompose flux differences to specific enzyme-level determinants.
next_steps: Phylogenetic reconstruction of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (mutA/mutB) copies across the panel; classify paralogs vs. orthologs.
Cross-reference PFOR/nifJ CDS with the PSHE PFREUD_RS00925 knockout target to test whether the 'same activity, different annotation' cases in the pathway audit are true isozymes or annotation drift.
Enzyme-constrained GEM (ecGEM) rebuild for at least PSHE and PPRO to test whether flux differences are stoichiometric (pathway architecture) or kinetic (enzyme abundance / kcat).

open_questions.q: How does CRISPR-Cas / anti-CRISPR loci content stratify across the pan-genome, and does phage-defense variation explain any of the 3,123 strain-specific clusters we recover in the 6-strain accessory-gene cloud?
open_questions.basis: Cutibacterium acnes is known to harbor a diverse Type I-E CRISPR-Cas system that segregates with phylotype (Marinelli et al., mBio 2012). The paper's pan-genome analysis does not annotate CRISPR arrays or anti-CRISPR proteins as a class, so their contribution to the accessory-gene cloud is unquantified. Phage-defense loci are known accessory-gene hotspots in skin commensals.
next_steps: Run CRISPRCasFinder / CCTyper on each of the 6 GBK files; catalog array count, spacer content, and cas-gene subtype per strain.
Scan the accessory-cluster set for AcrFinder / AcrCatalog anti-CRISPR homologs.
Cross-tabulate defense-locus presence with strain-specific vs. shell/cloud cluster membership to test whether phage-defense over-represents the accessory-gene tail.

open_questions.q: Do the accessory-gene sets in acne-associated Cutibacterium acnes phylotypes (IA-1, IA-2, IC) differ systematically from healthy-skin-associated phylotypes (II, III) in ways predictable from the McCubbin 2020 metabolic framework?
open_questions.basis: The paper analyzes P. acnes 6609 as a single representative of the species and does not stratify by phylotype or disease association. Fitz-Gibbon et al. (Journal of Investigative Dermatology 2013) established that specific C. acnes phylotypes (IA-1, IA-2, IC) are enriched in acne lesions while type II and III strains dominate healthy skin. If the paper's genome-scale metabolic framework generalizes, disease-associated phylotypes should show detectable metabolic-gene-content differences from health-associated ones.
next_steps: Pull >=20 C. acnes closed genomes with phylotype/disease annotation from BV-BRC / SRA-derived assemblies.
Recompute the accessory-gene cloud partitioned by phylotype and by disease/healthy label.

Build one GEM per phylotype (or gap-fill from PACN template) and test in silico whether acne-associated phylotypes show differential propionate, porphyrin, or lipase-pathway flux vs. healthy-skin phylotypes.
